Palisade is an educational, personal-development project. It is not a replacement for commercial application control products and comes with no support or warranty. Do not rely on it to protect production systems.

Palisade

Introduction

Palisade is an open-source, educational project for learning how application control works on Windows: deciding, before any code runs, whether it may run at all. It is written in Rust and built in public, design decisions and threat model included.

What application control is

Most endpoint security asks "is this file bad?". Application control asks a different question: "is this file one we approved?". An allowlist names the software an organisation approves, by cryptographic hash, by publisher certificate, or by a path that only administrators can write. Everything else is blocked by default: unknown executables, libraries, scripts, installers, drivers and the other object types the operating system can run. A blocklist removes dangerous exceptions from what an allowlist would otherwise allow, such as signed tools that are known to bypass the control.

Done well, application control stops most commodity malware and much hands-on-keyboard intrusion, because the attacker's tools are simply not on the list. Done badly, it either blocks the business or is quietly bypassed. Most of this book is about the details that decide which: how files are identified, how rules are combined, how changes are rolled out safely, and how a decision is explained afterwards.

Goals

  • Model the rule designs used across the application-control industry in one engine: hash, publisher, path and metadata rules, multi-condition rules, several precedence models, modes, group inheritance and unknown-application handling (Concepts).
  • Enforce through the operating system's own policy formats first, with an optional driver only for the gaps those formats leave (ADR 0002).
  • Explain every decision: which rule decided, which rules it overrode, and which facts were used.
  • Map the controls to the Australian Essential Eight and ISM as evidence (Compliance).
  • Practise careful engineering in the open: ADRs, a STRIDE threat model, fuzzing, supply-chain checks, and CI on GitHub-hosted runners only.

Non-goals

  • Replacing commercial application control products, or their support.
  • Production readiness. There is no service-level agreement, no supported-version promise and no security-fix timeline (ADR 0014).
  • Offensive tooling, real malware samples or bypass weaponisation (Responsible use).

Scope and status

Palisade is in milestone M0 (foundations). The policy model and evaluation engine, file identity (PE parsing, hashes, Authenticode, catalogs), the canonical event schema, the server skeleton and the repository tooling exist. The endpoint agent, OS-native policy compilation, the console and the REST API are still to come. The README has the milestone table. Pages in this book say plainly when they describe a design that is not built yet.

How this book is made

The book is built from the repository's own Markdown: docs/, the root policy files and every crate README. The reference pages are generated from the JSON Schemas and the command-line definitions the code uses, so they cannot drift. cargo xtask docs check fails CI when a generated page is stale. To build it locally, see Continuous integration: documentation site.

Source: docs/book/src/introduction.md on GitHub.

Concepts

These pages explain the ideas behind Palisade's policy model. Each one links the issue that specifies it in detail (the "E02" issues of the policy epic, #2) and the reference pages for the exact fields.

  • Identities: how a file is recognised (hash, publisher, path, metadata).
  • Rules and conditions: match trees, operators and actions.
  • Precedence models: which rule wins when several match.
  • Modes: audit, enforce, learning, monitor and disabled.
  • Groups and inheritance: how policy reaches a device.
  • Unknown applications: what happens when no rule decides.
  • Exceptions and offline overrides: workable default-deny.
  • Decision trace: explaining every decision.

The policy engine's own README, palisade-policy, is the detailed reference for what is implemented today.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/README.md on GitHub.

Identities

A rule says which objects it means through identity criteria: facts about the file itself. Specified in #31 (identity criteria) and #3 (how palisade-fileid computes them).

FamilyFieldsStrength
Hashhash.sha256, hash.sha384, hash.sha512, hash.authenticode_sha256strong: names exactly one file
Hash (compatibility)hash.sha1, hash.md5, hash.authenticode_sha1, page hashesweak alone (ADR 0008)
Publishersigner.publisher (CN, O or full DN)medium
Certificatesigner.leaf_thumbprint, signer.tbs_hashstrong: names one certificate (a TBS hash above the leaf names a CA, so it is weak in an allow)
Certificate authoritysigner.issuer, signer.pca, signer.root_thumbprint, signer.eku, SHA-1 thumbprintsweak alone: a CA vouches for every file it signs
Pathpath.full, path.directory, path.file_name, path.extensionmedium, and only where users cannot write
Metadatameta.original_filename, meta.product_name, meta.file_version, ...weak: easy to copy into another file

The strength matters. Validation warns about an allow rule whose only identity is weak, and an allow rule must have a positive identity on every branch of its match tree, so a rule cannot allow "anything not named X". A path rule only allows a file in a location that ordinary users cannot write (ISM-1392); the engine checks the path's ACL safety at evaluation time.

Hash rules are the most precise and the most work: every update needs a new rule. Publisher rules trust what a signer signs, optionally narrowed by product name and minimum version (ISM-1471: use publisher and product names). The publisher_product preset (palisade_policy::model::preset::PublisherProduct) builds that form. By default a signer criterion only trusts signatures that are valid, valid with an expired but timestamped certificate, or catalog-signed; a criterion's signer options can accept other statuses, require a timestamp after a date or a minimum key size, reject algorithms, or pick the signature's source and index. To block a stolen certificate, deny its signer.tbs_hash. That blocks one certificate only: the hashed data includes the serial number and the validity period, so a certificate reissued with the same key has a new TBS hash and needs its own rule. No criterion yet names a key across all the certificates that carry it. Path rules are the easiest to write and the easiest to get wrong.

A workstation baseline with hash, publisher and path rules (ISM-0955), validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# A workstation baseline with hash, publisher and path rules (ISM-0955).
# The same document as tests/fixtures/valid/workstation-baseline.json.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f
  name: Workstation baseline
  description: Hash, publisher and path rules for standard workstations.
  revision: 42
  precedence_model: deny_wins
  mode: enforce
  settings:
    script_control: audit
    script_control_by_kind:
      powershell: enforce
      vbscript: enforce
    dll_control: enforce
    driver_control: enforce
    capture_command_line: false
    poll_interval_secs: 900
    decision_cache_ttl_secs: 300
    override_durations: [15, 60, 240, 0, 1440]
    time_zone_basis: utc
    max_ancestor_depth: 8
    allow_unknown_advanced: false
  # Rule sets apply in this order.
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e60
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e70
  metadata:
    justification: Essential Eight application control baseline.
    ticket_ref: CHG-1001
    tags: [e8, workstation]

rule_sets:
  # A mandatory blocklist is checked before every other rule, in every mode.
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e60
    name: Recommended block rules
    version: "3.0"
    kind: blocklist
    mandatory: true
    read_only: true
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e61
        display_id: R-000001
        name: Block a known bypass binary
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: meta.original_filename
                operator: equals
                values: [example-bypass.exe]
            - criterion:
                field: meta.file_version
                operator: version_lt
                values: ["10.0.2"]
        action: {type: deny}
        enforcement_override: always_enforce

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e70
    name: Approved applications
    kind: allowlist
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e71
        display_id: R-000002
        name: Line-of-business tool by hash
        object_types: [executable, library]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values:
              - 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
              - 60303ae22b998861bce3b28f33eec1be758a213c86c93c076dbe9f558c11c752
        action: {type: allow}
        metadata:
          justification: Approved in CHG-0991.
          ticket_ref: CHG-0991

      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e72
        name: Publisher and product
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: signer.publisher
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Software Ltd]
            - criterion:
                field: meta.product_name
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Editor]
                case_sensitive: true
            # Never from a temporary folder, even when signed.
            - not:
                criterion:
                  field: path.directory
                  operator: wildcard
                  values: ['%TEMP%\**']
        action: {type: allow}

      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e73
        name: Audit scripts in the shared tools folder
        enabled: false
        object_types: [script.powershell, script.batch]
        match:
          any:
            - criterion:
                field: path.directory
                operator: starts_with
                values: ['%PROGRAMDATA%\Tools\']
            - criterion:
                field: path.extension
                operator: equals
                values: [ps1]
        action: {type: audit}
        order: 100500
        priority: -5

A publisher rule narrowed by product name and minimum version (ISM-1471):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# Finance workstations: allow one line-of-business suite by publisher,
# product and minimum version, and keep PowerShell in audit while scripts
# are reviewed. `signer.publisher` is the signer's common name (the `CN` of
# the leaf certificate's subject), not the whole distinguished name.
#
# Quote values that are text but look like other types: versions ("12.0"),
# and words such as "yes", "no", "on" and "off". Unquoted, the reader
# rejects them rather than guess what they mean.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f00
  name: Finance workstations
  revision: 3
  mode: enforce
  settings:
    script_control_by_kind:
      powershell: audit
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f10
  metadata:
    ticket_ref: CHG-1042
    tags: [env.prod, finance]

rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f10
    name: Finance applications
    kind: allowlist
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f11
        name: Example Ledger 12 and later
        object_types: [executable, library]
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: signer.publisher
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Accounting Pty Ltd]
            - criterion:
                field: meta.product_name
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Ledger]
            - criterion:
                field: meta.product_version
                operator: version_ge
                values: ["12.0.0.0"]
            # The admin console ships in the same product, so this rule
            # leaves it to the next one, which decides who may run it.
            - not:
                criterion:
                  field: meta.original_filename
                  operator: equals
                  values: [LedgerAdmin.exe]
        action: {type: allow}
        metadata:
          justification: Core line-of-business application.
          ticket_ref: CHG-1042
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f12
        name: Ledger admin console for administrators only
        # Context criteria narrow a rule; they never identify the object.
        # The publisher and file name identify it; the user's groups and
        # session decide who may run it. Group values are SIDs, not names.
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: signer.publisher
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Accounting Pty Ltd]
            - criterion:
                field: meta.original_filename
                operator: equals
                values: [LedgerAdmin.exe]
            - criterion:
                field: user.groups
                operator: member_of
                values: [S-1-5-32-544]
            - not:
                criterion:
                  field: session.is_remote
                  operator: is_true
        action: {type: allow}

See also: the full field list in the policy reference, and the file identity crate.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/identities.md on GitHub.

Rules and conditions

A rule is a match tree plus an action. Specified in #33 (condition trees), #32 (operators) and #34 (actions).

The tree combines criteria with all, any and not. Each criterion is field operator values: signer.publisher equals ["Example Software Ltd"]. Context criteria test the user, device and session (user.is_admin, device.tags, session.type) rather than the file, so a rule can say "this publisher, but only for members of this group".

Evaluation uses three-valued logic. A criterion on a fact that was not collected is unknown, and unknown never makes an allow match: an allow rule fails closed. A deny rule chooses, with unknown_as, whether unknown blocks.

Rules live in rule sets (allowlist, blocklist, baseline, trust, elevation, containment or mixed). A policy references rule sets by ID, so one rule set can be shared by many policies.

The actions are allow, deny, audit (an annotation, never a decision), allow_contained, allow_elevated, trust_source, ignore (a performance exclusion) and defer. Each rule can set effects: logging, upload, notification, severity and tags.

A complete example with every action, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# Rule actions and effect flags (#34). Each rule set kind holds the actions
# it is for; a `mixed` set holds any. Effect flags are optional: an unset
# flag takes the action's default (see the palisade-policy README).
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5000
  name: Actions and effects
  revision: 1
  mode: audit
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5010
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5020
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5030
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5040

rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5010
    name: Blocked tools
    kind: blocklist
    rules:
      # Block a tool, stop copies already running, and let the user ask for
      # an exception from a custom notification.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5011
        name: Block an unapproved remote-access tool
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: signer.publisher
            operator: equals
            values: ["CN=Example Remote Tools Ltd"]
        action:
          type: deny
          kill_running: true
          allow_request: true
        effects:
          notify: custom
          notification_text: "{file} is not approved here. Use the request button to ask IT."
          help_url: https://help.example/remote-access
          severity: high
          tags: [remote-access]

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5020
    name: Detections
    kind: mixed
    rules:
      # Audit rules never change the outcome: they tag the decision.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5021
        name: Flag programs started from Downloads
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: path.directory
            operator: starts_with
            values: ['%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\']
        action: {type: audit}
        effects:
          severity: low
          tags: [downloads]

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5030
    name: Administrator tasks
    kind: elevation
    rules:
      # Elevate one installer when it asks for administrator rights, after
      # the user gives a reason and authenticates again.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5031
        name: Elevate the printer driver installer
        object_types: [installer]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: [3f9a1c0d5e7b2a4c6e8f0a1b3c5d7e9f1a2b4c6d8e0f2a3b5c7d9e1f3a5b7c9d]
        action:
          type: allow_elevated
          token_profile: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f01
          condition: if_required
          reason_prompt: Why do you need to install this driver?
          auth: reauth

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5040
    name: Trusted installers
    kind: trust
    rules:
      # Files the software deployment agent and its child processes write
      # under Program Files become trusted (#9). `%PROGRAMFILES%` covers both
      # program-files directories. A separate allow rule lets the agent
      # itself run.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5041
        name: Trust the software deployment agent
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: signer.publisher
            operator: equals
            values: ["CN=Example Deployment Ltd"]
        action:
          type: trust_source
          mode: chained
          scope_paths: ['%PROGRAMFILES%\', 'D:\Apps\']
          tag_output: true

A scope narrows who, where and when a rule applies: users and groups, devices, network location, session type and time windows. Specified in #38. A scope never identifies the object, which is the match tree's job, and never widens a rule: a rule applies only when the policy's scope, its rule set's assignment scope and its own scope all match. An example, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# Rule scoping: who, where and when a rule applies. Scopes narrow a rule;
# they never identify the object, which is the match tree's job, and they
# never widen a rule. A rule applies only when the policy's scope, its rule
# set's assignment scopes and its own scope all match.
#
# - The policy applies to the corporate network only, a location profile
#   the agent evaluates on network changes and heartbeats.
# - The scripting set is assigned to every user but service accounts named
#   `svc_*`. A name pattern may only exclude principals from rules that
#   let an object run, because account names can be spoofed.
# - The script engine is allowed for administrators only, so it stays
#   blocked for unprivileged users (ISM-1491). A filtered (non-elevated)
#   administrator token does not count.
# - The trading tool runs only during market hours in Sydney, with a
#   warning and termination five minutes after close. It is closed on
#   public holidays, and one instance per session is allowed.
# - Remote desktop sessions are denied a file transfer tool, except on
#   jump hosts, and its use from the thin-client range is audited.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f00
  name: Scoped rules
  revision: 1
  mode: enforce
  settings:
    time_zone_basis: device_local
    group_cache_max_age_secs: 43200
  scope:
    network:
      include:
        - location_profile: corporate
  location_profiles:
    - name: corporate
      all:
        - dns_suffix: corp.example.org
        - server_reachable: true
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f10
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f20
  rule_set_scopes:
    - rule_set: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f10
      scopes:
        - principals:
            exclude:
              - user_pattern: '*\svc_*'

rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f10
    name: Scripting and trading
    kind: allowlist
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f11
        name: Script engine for administrators
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: ["9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"]
        action: {type: allow}
        scope:
          principals:
            include:
              - well_known: administrators
          sessions:
            types: [console, rdp]
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f12
        name: Trading tool during market hours
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: signer.publisher
            operator: equals
            values: [Example Markets Pty Ltd]
        action: {type: allow}
        scope:
          principals:
            include:
              - directory_group:
                  sid: S-1-5-21-1004336348-1177238915-682003330-1105
                  name: Traders
          max_instances_per_session: 1
          schedule:
            timezone_basis: device_local
            windows:
              - days: [mon, tue, wed, thu, fri]
                start: "10:00"
                end: "16:00"
            except_dates:
              - from: 2026-12-25
                to: 2026-12-26
              - from: 2027-01-01
            on_window_close: warn_then_terminate
            grace_secs: 300

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f20
    name: Remote session controls
    kind: blocklist
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f21
        name: No file transfer in remote sessions
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: ["60303ae22b998861bce3b28f33eec1be758a213c86c93c076dbe9f558c11c752"]
        action: {type: deny}
        scope:
          sessions:
            types: [rdp]
          devices:
            exclude:
              - tag: role=jump-host
        metadata:
          justification: Remote sessions may not copy files off the network.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5f22
        name: Audit file transfer from thin clients
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: ["60303ae22b998861bce3b28f33eec1be758a213c86c93c076dbe9f558c11c752"]
        action: {type: audit}
        scope:
          sessions:
            types: [rdp]
            client:
              ip: [10.50.0.0/16]
              hostname: ["THIN-*"]

Context criteria test who runs the object, where and when: the user's and device's organisational unit, the process's integrity level, the session, the network and the time of day. Specified in #32 and #33. Like a scope, they only narrow a rule: every rule still names the object by a hash, signer or path. An example, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# Context criteria narrow an identity: who runs the object, where and when
# (#32, #33). Every rule still names the object by a hash, signer or path;
# the context only narrows it.
#
# - A remote-support tool runs only from the corporate network, during
#   business hours on weekdays, and only for users in the IT support OU.
# - A build agent's helper runs only on build servers (OS build 22000 or
#   later) and at medium integrity or above.
# - Scripts are blocked in remote sessions from outside the office range.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5000
  name: Context criteria
  revision: 1
  mode: enforce
  settings:
    time_zone_basis: device_local
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5010

rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5010
    name: Context-narrowed rules
    kind: mixed
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5011
        name: Remote support in hours from the office
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: signer.publisher
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Remote Tools Ltd]
            - criterion:
                field: net.location
                operator: member_of
                values: [corporate]
            - criterion:
                field: time.weekday
                operator: weekday_in
                values: [mon, tue, wed, thu, fri]
            - criterion:
                field: time.local_time
                operator: time_between
                values: ["08:00", "18:00"]
            - criterion:
                field: user.ou
                operator: equals
                values: ["OU=IT Support,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=org"]
                include_sub_ous: true
        action: {type: allow}
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5012
        name: Build helper on build servers
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: hash.sha256
                operator: equals
                values: [9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08]
            - criterion:
                field: device.os_build
                operator: ge
                values: ["22000"]
            - criterion:
                field: user.integrity_level
                operator: ge
                values: [medium]
            - criterion:
                field: device.tags
                operator: all_of
                values: [build, env.prod]
        action: {type: allow}
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d5013
        name: No scripts from remote clients outside the office
        object_types: [script.powershell, script.vbscript]
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: path.extension
                operator: equals
                values: [ps1, vbs]
            - criterion:
                field: session.is_remote
                operator: is_true
            - not:
                criterion:
                  field: session.client_ip
                  operator: ip_in_cidr
                  values: [10.0.0.0/8, "2001:db8::/32"]
        action: {type: deny}

Rules also have a lifecycle and governance metadata: an activity window (activates_at, expires_at) with what happens on expiry (on_expire), a review date, an owner and a justification. Specified in #40. In governance mode, allow, trust and exception rules must carry that metadata, and exceptions must expire within a year. An example, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# Rule lifecycle and governance (#40). Governance mode is on, so every
# allow carries a justification and a review date, and the exception (a
# path allow for a vendor tool) also carries an expiry within a year, an
# approver and a risk rating. A temporary deny becomes an audit rule when it
# expires, so its matches are still recorded.
#
# The tenant raises `weak_identity` to an error, so the policy assistant
# reports the path exception as an error and the publish gate blocks the
# bundle until an administrator overrides it with a reason (see
# `tests/snapshots/lint/examples.txt`).
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f
  name: Governed rules
  revision: 1
  mode: enforce
  governance:
    require_justification: true
    stale_after_days: 90
    expiry_notice_days:
      - 14
      - 3
      - 0
    severity:
      weak_identity: error
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e60
rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e60
    name: Line-of-business
    kind: mixed
    metadata:
      owner: grp-desktop-engineering
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e61
        name: Payroll client
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: signer.publisher
                operator: equals
                values:
                  - Example Payroll Ltd
            - criterion:
                field: meta.product_name
                operator: equals
                values:
                  - Payroll Client
        action:
          type: allow
        metadata:
          owner: alice@example.org
          justification: Payroll processing for the finance team.
          ticket_ref: CHG-1042
          source: manual
          created_at: "2026-11-25T00:00:00Z"
          review_by: "2027-11-25"
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e62
        name: Vendor diagnostic tool (exception)
        expires_at: "2027-05-25T00:00:00Z"
        on_expire:
          delete_after_days: 30
        match:
          criterion:
            field: path.directory
            operator: starts_with
            values:
              - C:\VendorTools\Diag
        action:
          type: allow
        metadata:
          justification: Vendor support needs this tool until the next release.
          approved_by: ciso@example.org
          approved_at: "2026-11-25T00:00:00Z"
          created_at: "2026-11-25T00:00:00Z"
          risk_rating: medium
          compensating_controls: Folder ACL limited to administrators; reviewed quarterly.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e63
        name: Block the old installer during the migration
        activates_at: "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"
        expires_at: "2027-03-01T00:00:00Z"
        on_expire: convert_to_audit
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values:
              - aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        action:
          type: deny

See also: Rule, Match, Criterion and Action in the policy reference.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/rules-and-conditions.md on GitHub.

Precedence models

A file often matches several rules: a publisher allow and a path deny, say. The precedence model decides which wins. Specified in #35 and ADR 0004.

Evaluation runs in fixed stages, whatever the model:

  1. Mandatory deny. A matching rule of a mandatory blocklist blocks, in every mode and every override session. Nothing overrides it.
  2. Exclusion. A matching ignore rule makes the object ignored.
  3. Policy. The policy's precedence_model chooses among the matching allows and denies.
  4. Unknown. If nothing decided, the implicit deny (Unknown applications).
ModelDecides
deny_wins (default)any matching deny; otherwise an allow
allow_winsany matching allow; otherwise a deny (not recommended for Essential Eight)
specificitythe rule with the most specific identity (hash beats publisher beats path)
first_matchthe lowest order
prioritythe winning numeric priority

Decisions are deterministic: every tie ends on the unique rule ID, so shuffling rule sets or rules never changes a decision. The decision names the deciding rule and every rule it overrode.

An example under first_match, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# A firewall-style policy: rules are ordered, and the first rule that
# matches and does not defer decides (#35). Curated rule sets come first
# (curated_first, the default). The mandatory blocklist is checked before
# every ordered rule, whatever its order.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f
  name: Ordered build servers
  revision: 1
  precedence_model: first_match
  mode: enforce
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e60
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e70

rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e60
    name: Never run
    kind: blocklist
    mandatory: true
    read_only: true
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e61
        name: Known bypass tool
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: [aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa]
        action:
          type: deny

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e70
    name: Build tools
    kind: mixed
    rules:
      # Custom rules use orders 100001 to 999989.
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e71
        name: Not decided by the toolchain rule
        match:
          criterion:
            field: signer.publisher
            operator: equals
            values: [Example Compilers Ltd]
        # No opinion: evaluation falls through to the next rule.
        action:
          type: defer
        order: 100100
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e72
        name: Old compiler builds
        match:
          all:
            - criterion:
                field: signer.publisher
                operator: equals
                values: [Example Compilers Ltd]
            - criterion:
                field: meta.file_version
                operator: version_lt
                values: ["4.0"]
        # A file version that is not a version counts as old.
        action:
          type: deny
          on_unparseable: match
        order: 100200
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e73
        name: Compilers
        match:
          criterion:
            field: signer.publisher
            operator: equals
            values: [Example Compilers Ltd]
        action:
          type: allow
        order: 100300

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/precedence.md on GitHub.

Modes

The mode decides whether a decision takes effect. Specified in #36.

ModeEffect
disabledThe engine is not consulted. Only a whole device can be disabled.
monitorEvaluate fully, allow everything, report what would have been blocked.
auditAs monitor, with a full event for every decision.
learningAs audit, and every object only the implicit deny would block becomes a learning candidate.
enforceBlocked means blocked.

A safe rollout moves from audit to enforce in steps: per object type (mode_by_type, for example scripts still in audit while executables are enforced), per rule set (mode_override on a new blocklist), and per rule (enforcement_override). A device that has been offline too long can switch to a stricter mode_disconnected. Leaving enforce is time-boxed, needs a reason, and reverts automatically, even if the clock is set back.

A mandatory deny blocks in every mode. Only a disabled device skips it.

A staged rollout, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# A staged rollout (#36): the policy is in audit, so what it would block is
# reported but runs. Executables are already enforced, a disconnected
# device enforces everything, and a new blocklist is tried in monitor
# mode. The mandatory blocklist blocks in every mode, and one deny rule is
# enforced in audit too (`always_enforce`).
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f20
  name: Staged rollout
  revision: 1
  mode: audit
  mode_options:
    mode_by_type:
      executable: enforce
    mode_disconnected: enforce
    disconnected_after_secs: 3600
  rule_sets:
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f30
    - 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f40

rule_sets:
  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f30
    name: Never run
    kind: blocklist
    mandatory: true
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f31
        name: Known bypass tool
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: [aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa]
        action:
          type: deny

  - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f40
    name: Trial blocklist
    kind: blocklist
    # Report only, whatever the object's mode.
    mode_override: monitor
    rules:
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f41
        name: Remote access tool
        match:
          criterion:
            field: signer.publisher
            operator: equals
            values: [Example Remote Ltd]
        action:
          type: deny
      - id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4f42
        name: Retired script host
        object_types: [executable]
        match:
          criterion:
            field: hash.sha256
            operator: equals
            values: [bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb]
        action:
          type: deny
        # Enforced even though its rule set only reports.
        enforcement_override: always_enforce

The audit-to-enforce walkthrough is in Getting started.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/modes.md on GitHub.

Groups and inheritance

A policy reaches a device through a hierarchy of scopes: global, tenant, nested groups, and the device itself. Specified in #37; the engine side is built (hierarchy and library in palisade-policy). The server and console that manage the hierarchy are milestone M3 (#129).

Each level can add rule sets and change settings, and a level can lock a setting so lower levels cannot weaken it. Groups nest at most 8 deep; built-in groups catch devices that are unassigned, unmanaged or in staging, and dynamic groups and placement rules put devices in groups automatically.

Reusable libraries (rule sets, application definitions, match fragments, and hash, publisher, path, principal, device, network and schedule sets) are referenced by ID and version pin rather than copied, so a fix in one place reaches every policy that uses it. A ref node in a match tree names one; reference cycles are rejected.

The output is one deterministic effective policy per device: a pure function of the hierarchy, the libraries at their resolved versions and the device's dynamic groups, with the provenance of every rule and setting and a content hash. The engine only ever evaluates an effective policy, so everything in Rules and Precedence applies unchanged.

Rule scoping by user, group, device, time, network and session is specified in #38.

See also: LibraryRef and Match in the policy reference.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/groups-and-inheritance.md on GitHub.

Unknown applications

When no rule decides, the unknown-application policy (policy.unknown) does. Specified in #39. It never overrides an explicit allow or deny.

By default it applies the implicit deny: anything not explicitly allowed is blocked (in enforce mode) or reported (in audit, monitor and learning). The decision's reason code is implicit_deny_unknown, so reports can tell "blocked by a rule" from "never allowed".

The smallest policy shows the implicit deny on its own, validated in CI:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# The smallest valid policy: no rule sets, so nothing is allowed and every
# file is reported (audit mode) by the implicit deny.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f
  name: Minimal audit policy
  revision: 1
  mode: audit

Levels and overrides

A policy can choose a level other than block for unknown objects: restrict (run in a containment profile), prompt (ask the user), detect (allow and report) or allow. It can set that level per object type, per location class (user_profile, temp, program_files, removable, network and others) and per origin (internet, email_attachment, removable_copy and others). The most restrictive matching entry wins, and default applies when none matches. The Essential Eight presets e8_ml1 to e8_ml3 set a documented starting point, and validation warns when a policy is weaker than its preset.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# Unknown-application handling (#39), starting from the Essential Eight
# maturity level 1 preset: unknown objects in user profiles, temporary
# folders and other user-writable locations are blocked, and elsewhere they
# are detected.
#
# The level applied is the most restrictive entry that matches, so the
# overrides below only apply where no stricter entry does:
# - A download (`internet`) is contained rather than detected, except in a
#   user profile, temporary folder or other user-writable location, where
#   `block` outranks `restrict`.
# - An unknown PowerShell script asks the user, falling back to block, only
#   where nothing stricter matches: a downloaded script in a program folder
#   is contained (`restrict` outranks `prompt`), and one in a user profile
#   is blocked.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f
  name: Unknown application handling
  revision: 1
  mode: enforce
  unknown:
    preset: e8_ml1
    default: detect
    by_location:
      user_profile: block
      temp: block
      user_writable_other: block
    by_origin:
      internet: restrict
    by_type:
      script.powershell: prompt
    restrict_profile: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d0c01
    prompt:
      options:
        - allow_once
        - allow_always_local
        - request_approval
        - block
      require_justification: true
      timeout_secs: 60
      fallback: block
    effects:
      severity: high
      tags:
        - unhandled

Missing facts never make an object look safer

The endpoint agent supplies the facts stage 6 decides on: the path variables, the volume a file is on, and where the file came from. If one is missing, the engine does not guess. A location class or origin that the missing fact could make true is treated as possible, and its level applies too. A missing fact can therefore make a decision stricter, never looser. The decision lists the missing facts, and the explanation names them.

If the agent sends no origin facts at all, every origin is possible. Under the default preexisting_policy: baseline_only, that blocks every unknown object in enforce mode.

The full rules, including scopes, inheritance and the built-in system_baseline, are in the policy crate's README.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/unknown-applications.md on GitHub.

Exceptions and offline overrides

Planned. Trust sources and overrides are designed in epic #9. The policy engine already defines how an override session changes a decision; issuing one is not built yet.

A default-deny policy needs principled ways to say yes without weakening it:

  • Trust sources (#114): trust a file by how it arrived, for example written by a trusted installer or updater. The trust_source action grants this, direct or chained through child processes.
  • Owner-based trust (#117): trust files owned by a trusted principal.
  • Offline override codes (#120): a time-boxed, device-bound, audited code for when the server cannot be reached.
  • Challenge/response and install windows (#121, #123).

One invariant holds throughout: the mandatory blocklist always wins (#125). An override session lowers the mode of ordinary rules to audit; it never lets through what a mandatory deny blocks.

The Essential Eight requires that users cannot disable or bypass application control (ISM-0846). Every override is therefore logged, bounded in time and scope, and reported as allowed_override.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/exceptions-and-overrides.md on GitHub.

Decision trace

Every decision must be explainable. Specified in #41; the engine side is built (trace in palisade-policy).

Every Decision carries:

  • the outcome (allowed, blocked, allowed_audit, allowed_override, ignored) and the enforce-mode outcome (would_have_been);
  • the deciding rule and every rule it overrode;
  • audit annotations, trust-source grants and the effective mode;
  • a reason code (for example mandatory_deny or implicit_deny_unknown) and a trace ID.

A trace records how that decision was reached, at a level the agent chooses (minimal for an object that runs, standard for a block or would-block, full while diagnosing):

  • how the mode was resolved, and which pipeline stages decided, passed or were skipped;
  • every rule that matched and its role, and each of the deciding rule's criteria with its result;
  • every fact that was missing or untrusted, and what that did;
  • the rules that nearly matched, with the criteria that failed;
  • for a block, a draft allow rule from the strongest identity available, which the engine never applies itself.

Every list in a trace is bounded, and user, device and session values are withheld by default (an HMAC digest can stand in for them).

Explain turns a trace into text for the CLI, the console and the tray: a summary, a reason a person can act on, "why not allowed?" and "what would allow this?".

Simulate replays recorded facts against the current policy and a candidate (a draft, a set of rule changes, or a mode change such as audit to enforce) and reports what would change. The same machinery runs policy-as-code tests and the readiness report for moving to enforce; see the simulation examples.

Decisions become events in the canonical event schema; see the event reference.

Source: docs/book/src/concepts/decision-trace.md on GitHub.

Simulation examples

Policy-as-code tests and recorded facts for ../policies/staged-rollout.yaml (#41).

  • staged-rollout.tests.yaml: given facts and the decision each must get. cargo test -p palisade-policy --test simulation runs them, so CI fails when the policy and its tests disagree. The pal policy test command (#15) will read the same files and write JUnit XML.
  • staged-rollout.snapshots.yaml: decision inputs as an agent records them, in the facts_schema_version 1 format. The same test replays them under the policy, and again under the policy moved to enforce. It then checks the readiness report: how many would-block events each device had, and whether the move needs a readiness_ack.

Source: docs/examples/simulation/README.md on GitHub.

Getting started

Palisade is not usable as a product yet (see the Introduction). What you can do today is build it, write and validate policies, and run the policy engine's tests and examples.

  • Lab install: build from source, and the planned disposable-VM lab.
  • Your first policy: write a policy, validate it, and plan the audit-to-enforce rollout.

Source: docs/book/src/getting-started/README.md on GitHub.

Lab install

Only on machines you own and can throw away. Palisade is educational software (ADR 0014).

Build from source

You need rustup and Git; the toolchain is pinned in rust-toolchain.toml.

git clone https://github.com/jusso-dev/palisade.git
cd palisade
cargo build --workspace --exclude palisade-driver
cargo test --workspace --exclude palisade-driver

The full build instructions, for Windows and other platforms, are in the README.

The VM lab

Planned. The Windows VM integration test harness is #26 (milestone M1).

The harness will create a disposable Windows virtual machine from a local hypervisor, install the agent from the MSI (#22), enrol it with a local server, run benign test executables and scripts, and reset the VM afterwards. Until it lands there is no supported way to install the agent: the agent binary runs in the foreground with palisade-agent --console (see the CLI reference), but does not enforce anything yet.

Source: docs/book/src/getting-started/lab-install.md on GitHub.

Your first policy

Policies are YAML (or JSON) documents checked against the policy schema. The first line names the schema, so an editor with the YAML language server completes field names and flags mistakes.

Write it

Start from the smallest valid policy. It has no rule sets, so the implicit deny reports every file, and mode: audit means nothing is blocked:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusso-dev/palisade/main/schemas/policy/v1.json
#
# The smallest valid policy: no rule sets, so nothing is allowed and every
# file is reported (audit mode) by the implicit deny.
schema_version: "1.0.0"
policy:
  id: 01936b2e-8c4a-7b3d-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f
  name: Minimal audit policy
  revision: 1
  mode: audit

Then add an allowlist rule set with hash, publisher and path rules, as in the workstation baseline.

Validate it

The policy engine's tests check every example in docs/examples/policies/ against the committed schema, load it, and run full validation, which reports every finding with a code, a JSON Pointer and a line and column:

cargo test -p palisade-policy --test yaml

To check your own file the same way, add it to docs/examples/policies/ and run that test. A pal policy validate command arrives with the CLI (#189).

From audit to enforce

  1. Audit. Deploy in audit mode. Every decision is logged, and what enforce mode would block is reported as allowed_audit with would_have_been: blocked.
  2. Review. Turn the would-block reports into rules, or confirm they should stay blocked. Learning mode marks objects that only the implicit deny would block as candidates (#5).
  3. Enforce by type. Enforce executables first with mode_by_type, while scripts stay in audit. Try new blocklists with mode_override: audit.
  4. Enforce. Switch the policy to enforce. Leaving enforce later is time-boxed and reverts on its own (Modes).

The staged-rollout example on the Modes page shows steps 3 and 4 in one document.

Source: docs/book/src/getting-started/first-policy.md on GitHub.

Palisade policy document

A versioned policy document: one policy and the rule sets it uses.

Schema: schemas/policy/v1.json ($id https://github.com/jusso-dev/palisade/schemas/policy/v1.json), version 1.0.0. Regenerate the schema with PALISADE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p palisade-policy --test schema, then these pages with cargo xtask docs generate.

Fields

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
policyPolicyyes1.0.0The policy.
rule_setsarray of RuleSetnoat most 1000 items1.0.0The rule sets the policy references, in any order. The policy's rule_sets list gives the order that applies.
schema_versionSchemaVersionyes1.0.0The version of this schema the document was written for. A reader accepts the same major version and any minor version.

Object types

  • Action: The action of a rule (#34).
  • ClientFilter: The client connected to a remote desktop session, for per-client scoping on multi-session hosts. Each list that is set must match.
  • CloudObject: An object in a cloud directory: a group of users or of devices.
  • Criterion: A test of one fact about the object or its context: field operator values.
  • DateRange: An inclusive range of dates. to unset means the single day from.
  • DeviceRef: A device or group of devices (#38).
  • DirectoryGroup: A directory group.
  • Effects: The effect flags of one rule. Unset fields take the action's default.
  • GovernanceSettings: The tenant's governance settings (#40). Every field is optional.
  • LibraryRef: A reference to a library from a match tree or a hierarchy assignment.
  • LocationProfile: A named network location, such as corporate: every test must match (#38). The agent evaluates the profiles when the network changes and on every heartbeat, and scopes test the result with location_profile.
  • Match: A condition tree (#33).
  • Metadata: Governance metadata (#40), on a policy, a rule set or a rule. Every field is optional. Metadata is not decision-relevant: it never changes what a rule decides (PolicyDocument::decision_relevant).
  • ModeOptions: Mode settings besides the base mode. Each is optional in a document.
  • NetworkRef: A network location test (#38). Address tests match when any local interface address does.
  • OnExpire: What happens when a rule expires.
  • OuRef: A directory organisational unit.
  • Policy: The decision part of a policy: which rule sets apply, and how.
  • PolicySettings: Settings that apply to the whole policy. Every field is optional in a document and has the default shown in the schema.
  • PrecedenceOptions: Settings of the precedence models. Each is optional in a document.
  • PrincipalRef: A user or group (#38). Each is an object with one key, the kind.
  • PromptSettings: How the prompt level asks the user.
  • RefList: An include and an exclude list. An empty include means every entry; a match in exclude always wins.
  • RefList2: An include and an exclude list. An empty include means every entry; a match in exclude always wins.
  • RefList3: An include and an exclude list. An empty include means every entry; a match in exclude always wins.
  • Rule: One rule: a match tree and the action taken when it matches.
  • RuleSet: A named, reusable, ordered collection of rules.
  • RuleSetScope: The scopes of one rule-set assignment: every one must match for the set's rules to apply.
  • Schedule: When a scope is active (#38).
  • Scope: Who, where and when a rule applies (#38).
  • ScopeLimit: One contributing policy's limit on where its unknown settings apply, in an effective policy (UnknownPolicy::scope_limits). It holds when every scope of all_of matches and, if any_of is not empty, one of its scopes matches.
  • SessionFilter: Session criteria (#38).
  • SignerOptions: The options of a signer criterion (#31).
  • UnknownPolicy: The unknown-application policy (#39). Every field is optional in a document; the defaults block every unknown object.
  • Window: One weekly window.

Enumerations and string formats: Value types.

Examples

Each example passes this schema and full validation (cargo test -p palisade-policy --test yaml, in CI).

  • actions-and-effects.yaml: Rule actions and effect flags (#34). Each rule set kind holds the actions it is for; a mixed set holds any. Effect flags are optional: an unset flag takes the action's default (see the palisade-policy README).
  • context-criteria.yaml: Context criteria narrow an identity: who runs the object, where and when (#32, #33). Every rule still names the object by a hash, signer or path; the context only narrows it.
  • finance-workstations.yaml: Finance workstations: allow one line-of-business suite by publisher, product and minimum version, and keep PowerShell in audit while scripts are reviewed. signer.publisher is the signer's common name (the CN of the leaf certificate's subject), not the whole distinguished name.
  • first-match.yaml: A firewall-style policy: rules are ordered, and the first rule that matches and does not defer decides (#35). Curated rule sets come first (curated_first, the default). The mandatory blocklist is checked before every ordered rule, whatever its order.
  • minimal.yaml: The smallest valid policy: no rule sets, so nothing is allowed and every file is reported (audit mode) by the implicit deny.
  • rule-lifecycle.yaml: Rule lifecycle and governance (#40). Governance mode is on, so every allow carries a justification and a review date, and the exception (a path allow for a vendor tool) also carries an expiry within a year, an approver and a risk rating. A temporary deny becomes an audit rule when it expires, so its matches are still recorded.
  • scoped-rules.yaml: Rule scoping: who, where and when a rule applies. Scopes narrow a rule; they never identify the object, which is the match tree's job, and they never widen a rule. A rule applies only when the policy's scope, its rule set's assignment scopes and its own scope all match.
  • staged-rollout.yaml: A staged rollout (#36): the policy is in audit, so what it would block is reported but runs. Executables are already enforced, a disconnected device enforces everything, and a new blocklist is tried in monitor mode. The mandatory blocklist blocks in every mode, and one deny rule is enforced in audit too (always_enforce).
  • unknown-applications.yaml: Unknown-application handling (#39), starting from the Essential Eight maturity level 1 preset: unknown objects in user profiles, temporary folders and other user-writable locations are blocked, and elsewhere they are detected.
  • workstation-baseline.yaml: A workstation baseline with hash, publisher and path rules (ISM-0955). The same document as tests/fixtures/valid/workstation-baseline.json.

Source: docs/book/src/reference/generated/policy/index.md on GitHub.

Action

The action of a rule (#34).

Each action is an object with a type, and its options as optional keys, so options can be added later without a breaking change.

Appears at: /rule_sets/rules/action.

Variants

type: allow

Permit execution.

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
typeconstantyesalways "allow"1.0.0

type: deny

Block execution.

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
allow_requestbooleanno1.0.0The end user may raise an approval request (#11). Needs a notification, and is not valid in a mandatory rule set.
kill_runningbooleanno1.0.0Terminate already-running instances that match when the policy is applied. Not valid for drivers or libraries.
on_unparseableUnknownAsno1.0.0Whether a version fact that is not a version counts towards the rule applying (#32, #35). With match, each version criterion on such a fact is taken in whichever direction makes the deny apply, also under not. The rest of the tree is evaluated as usual. no_match, the default, leaves the criterion Unknown, which unknown_as then decides.
request_templateRequestTemplateRefno1.0.0The approval request template to use. Only with allow_request.
typeconstantyesalways "deny"1.0.0
unknown_asUnknownAsno1.0.0Whether the rule blocks when its match tree is Unknown because a fact is missing or cannot be trusted (#32, #35). no_match, the default, means an unknown fact does not block; match makes the deny fail closed.

type: audit

Record the match without changing the outcome. A non-terminal annotation, used for detection and tagging.

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
typeconstantyesalways "audit"1.0.0

type: allow_contained

Permit execution inside a containment profile (#14). The engine only carries the reference.

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
profile_idContainmentProfileRefyes1.0.0The containment profile the process runs under.
typeconstantyesalways "allow_contained"1.0.0

typeconstantyesalways "allow_elevated"1.0.0

Mark the matching process as a trusted installer, updater or source (#9, #114). This does not permit the process itself to run; an allow rule decides that. The engine returns the directive.

Criterion

A test of one fact about the object or its context: field operator values.

Values are combined with OR for positive operators and with AND for negative ones (#32): not_contains [a, b] means neither a nor b.

Appears at: /rule_sets/rules/match/all/all/all/criterion, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/all/any/criterion, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/all/not/criterion, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/all/criterion, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/any/all/criterion, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/any/any/criterion, and more.

Fields

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
anchoredbooleanno1.0.0Only for regex and not_regex: false lets the pattern match anywhere in the fact instead of the whole fact (#32). Unset means true.
case_sensitivebooleanno1.0.0Compare strings case-sensitively. Unset means the field's default (#32), which is case-insensitive for every field defined so far. Only text, paths, file names, account names and tags have a case; other fields (hashes, versions, SIDs, group sets, yes-or-no facts and session types) reject this option.
fieldFieldyes1.0.0The fact being tested.
include_sub_ousbooleanno1.0.0Only for user.ou and device.ou: true also matches objects in every organisational unit below the named one (#33). Unset means false: the object must be directly in it.
match_adsbooleanno1.0.0Only for positive tests of path.full: true lets a value that names no alternate data stream also match a stream of a file it matches, so C:\\Tools\\* matches C:\\Tools\\a.exe:s (#32). Unset means false: a stream is its own object.
operatorOperatoryes1.0.0How it is compared.
safety_criticalbooleanno1.0.0Only in a mandatory blocklist: when the fact is unknown, this criterion counts towards the deny applying (match, or no_match under an odd number of not nodes), so the shipped blocklists fail closed (#32, #87). Unset means false.
signerSignerOptionsno1.0.0Only for signer.* fields: which signatures take part, and what each must also satisfy (#31). The options bind to the signature the field is read from, so min_key_bits on a publisher test needs the publisher's own signature to have the key size. Unset means every option's default.
valuesarray of stringnoat most 25 items1.0.01 to 25 values. Each is at most 2048 bytes of UTF-8; the schema can only bound the length in characters, so validation checks the bytes. is_true and is_false take no values, and the key may be left out.

Schedule

When a scope is active (#38).

Times are wall-clock times in the schedule's time zone. A window starts on one of its days at start and lasts until end (which may be on the next day: 22:00 to 06:00 wraps midnight) or for duration_mins. With no windows, every time of day is in. dates and except_dates test the local date of the moment being decided.

Appears at: /policy/rule_set_scopes/scopes/schedule, /policy/scope/schedule, /policy/unknown/scope_limits/all_of/schedule, /policy/unknown/scope_limits/any_of/schedule, /policy/unknown/scopes/schedule, /rule_sets/rules/scope/schedule.

SignerOptions

The options of a signer criterion (#31).

A signer criterion matches if any signature that takes part satisfies it. A signature takes part when its status is accepted, it comes from the chosen source and has the chosen index, and it meets every constraint here (signed_after, countersigned, min_key_bits and disallowed_algorithms). A constraint whose fact is unknown makes that signature's result unknown, never a match.

Appears at: /rule_sets/rules/match/all/all/criterion/signer, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/any/criterion/signer, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/not/not/criterion/signer, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/not/criterion/signer, /rule_sets/rules/match/all/criterion/signer, /rule_sets/rules/match/any/all/criterion/signer, and more.

Fields

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultConstraintsSinceDescription
accept_statusarray of SignerStatusno1 to 6 items1.0.0The signature statuses that can match. Unset means valid, valid_expired_timestamped and catalog_signed. digest_mismatch cannot be listed: see allow_digest_mismatch. Validation warns when a rule that lets an object run accepts any other status.
allow_digest_mismatchbooleanno1.0.0Let a signature whose signed digest does not match the file take part: the file was changed after it was signed. Validation always warns about it. Unset means false.
componentSubjectComponentno1.0.0Only for signer.publisher: the part of the leaf subject compared. Unset means cn.
countersignedbooleanno1.0.0The signature must carry an RFC 3161 timestamp that verifies. Unset means false: no requirement.
disallowed_algorithmsarray of DigestAlgorithmnoat most 6 items1.0.0The signature must use none of these digest algorithms, in the file digest, the signer information or any certificate of its chain.
min_key_bitsintegerno1 to 16384; format uint321.0.0Every key in the signature's chain must be at least this strong, in RSA-equivalent bits (see crate::facts::KeyFact::rsa_equivalent_bits).
positionTbsPositionno1.0.0Only for signer.tbs_hash: where in the chain the certificate must be. Unset means any.
signature_indexintegerno0 to 63; format uint81.0.0Only the signature at this index, counted from 0 among the signatures of source: 0 is the primary embedded signature, 1 the first nested one. Unset means any signature.
signed_afterstringno1 to 64 characters1.0.0A trusted timestamp must show that the signature was made at or after this instant: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, such as 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z. A signature with no trusted timestamp is unknown.
sourceSignerSourceno1.0.0Where the signature must come from. Unset means any.

Unknown fields are rejected.

Value types

Enumerations, identifiers and string formats used by the Palisade policy document.

AdvancedValue

A scalar value in advanced.

Type: boolean or integer or string.

AllowTiebreak

Which allow decides among allows of different kinds.

ValueMeaning
most_restrictiveallow_contained, then allow, then allow_elevated (with condition: always before if_required). The default.
most_permissiveThe reverse: allow_elevated (if_required before always), then allow, then allow_contained.

ApprovalScope

Who a device-local approval applies to.

ValueMeaning
userOnly the user who approved it. The default.
deviceEvery user of the device.

Combine

How a scope's dimensions combine.

ValueMeaning
allEvery dimension that is set must match. The default.
anyAt least one dimension that is set must match.

CompliancePreset

A compliance preset: a named starting configuration. Changes that make the policy weaker than its preset raise a compliance warning (#17). Ordered from the least to the most demanding.

ValueMeaning
e8_ml1Essential Eight maturity level 1: block in user profiles, temporary folders and other user-writable locations, detect elsewhere (ISM-1870).
e8_ml2Essential Eight maturity level 2: block in every location (ISM-1871).
e8_ml3Essential Eight maturity level 3: level 2, drivers blocked, and a mandatory blocklist required (ISM-1658). Drivers loaded during early boot are only audited unless driver_boot_policy is enforce; validation warns about that exemption.

ContainmentProfileRef

The ID of a containment profile (#14, #173).

Type: Uuid7.

ControlLevel

Whether a class of object is controlled.

ValueMeaning
offNot evaluated.
auditEvaluated, and would-block decisions are reported only.
enforceEvaluated and enforced.

Date

A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD.

Type: string; matches ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

DigestAlgorithm

A digest algorithm a signature uses (#31, ADR 0008).

ValueMeaning
md2MD2.
md5MD5.
sha1SHA-1.
sha256SHA-256.
sha384SHA-384.
sha512SHA-512.

DriverBootPolicy

How unknown drivers are handled while the device boots, before the agent has fully started (boot_phase: early).

ValueMeaning
auditReport what would be blocked, and block nothing. The default, until the tenant enables enforcement explicitly.
enforceApply the unknown-handling level.

ElevationAuth

The confirmation an allow_elevated action asks for.

ValueMeaning
noneNo confirmation. The default.
reauthThe user authenticates again.
mfaThe user completes a multi-factor challenge.

ElevationCondition

When an allow_elevated action elevates.

ValueMeaning
alwaysEvery time the object runs.
if_requiredOnly when the object asks for administrator rights.

EnforcementOverride

How one rule relates to the policy mode (#36).

ValueMeaning
inheritFollow the effective mode. The default.
always_enforceEnforce this rule even in audit or learning mode.
never_enforceNever enforce this rule: it only reports what it would block.

EventSeverity

How serious an event is (#16).

ValueMeaning
infoInformational.
lowLow.
mediumMedium.
highHigh.
criticalCritical.

Field

The identity facts a criterion can test (#31).

This is the part of the #31 catalogue that has a matcher: hashes, the signer and its certificates, the path and the version resource. The other families (packaged apps, installers, ownership, origin and process relationships) arrive in later minor versions, each with its facts and matcher.

ValueMeaning
hash.sha256SHA-256 of the whole file. The primary identity (ADR 0008).
hash.sha384SHA-384 of the whole file.
hash.sha512SHA-512 of the whole file.
hash.authenticode_sha256SHA-256 Authenticode image hash: the PE image without its checksum, security directory entry and certificate table.
hash.authenticode_sha1SHA-1 Authenticode image hash. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
hash.page_sha256SHA-256 hash of the first page of the image, for OS-native policy formats. It covers only that page, so it is a weak identity alone.
hash.page_sha1SHA-1 hash of the first page of the image. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
hash.msi_fuzzy_sha256SHA-256 of an installer package with its timestamps left out, so rebuilds of the same content share one value (#3).
hash.sha1SHA-1 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
hash.md5MD5 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).

session.client_hostnameContext (#33): the host name of the client connected to the session, on a multi-session host.
session.is_remoteContext (#33): the session is remote.
user.integrity_levelContext (#33): the integrity level of the process token: untrusted, low, medium, medium_plus, high, system or protected. Ordered, so ge and le compare levels.
user.ouContext (#33): the organisational unit of the user's directory object, as a distinguished name such as OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=example. With include_sub_ous, units below it match too.
device.ouContext (#33): the organisational unit of the device's directory object, as for user.ou.
device.os_buildContext (#33): the operating system build number, such as 22631.
session.idContext (#33): the session ID.
session.client_ipContext (#33): the IP address of the client connected to the session, on a multi-session host.
net.ipContext (#33): every local interface address. A network test (ip_in_cidr, ip_between, ip_wildcard) matches if any address does; a set test holds the addresses as a set, so all_of needs every listed address to be present.
net.macContext (#33): every local interface MAC address.
net.dns_suffixContext (#33): every connection-specific DNS suffix.
net.connected_to_serverContext (#33): the device can reach its server now.
net.locationContext (#33, #38): the names of the network locations the device is in, such as corporate, remote or offline.
time.weekdayContext (#33): the day of the week of the evaluation, as mon to sun, in the clock the policy's time_zone_basis names.
time.local_timeContext (#33): the time of day of the evaluation, as HH:MM, in the policy's clock.
time.dateContext (#33): the date of the evaluation, as YYYY-MM-DD, in the policy's clock.
signer.leaf_thumbprint_sha1The SHA-1 thumbprint of the leaf certificate. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
signer.pcaThe subject common name of the highest certificate below the root, as the signature provides it: the PCA.
signer.root_thumbprintThe SHA-256 thumbprint of the chain's root certificate.
signer.root_thumbprint_sha1The SHA-1 thumbprint of the chain's root certificate. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
signer.tbs_hashThe hash of a chain certificate's tbsCertificate, under the certificate's own signature digest (40, 64, 96 or 128 hex digits). It identifies that one certificate: the tbsCertificate includes the serial number and the validity period (RFC 5280), so a certificate reissued with the same key has another TBS hash, and each issue needs its own rule. No criterion yet names a key across the certificates that carry it. signer.position says which certificate. A 40-digit (SHA-1) value is compatibility only (ADR 0008).
signer.ekuThe extended key usages of the leaf certificate, as dotted OIDs, such as 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3 (code signing). A leaf without the extension has none.

FindingSeverity

How serious a policy-assistant finding is (#40).

ValueMeaning

warningProbably a mistake or a risk.

Level

How an unknown object is handled. The variants are declared from least to most restrictive, so Ord is the restrictiveness order.

ValueMeaning
allowAllowed silently. Validation warns, and Essential Eight presets do not permit it for user profiles or temporary folders.
detectAllowed, but logged with severity medium and flagged unhandled.
promptThe user is asked (#11). Not for libraries, drivers, objects that a blocklist matched, or sessions with no interactive user; those get the prompt's fallback.
restrictAllowed inside the restrict_profile containment profile (#14). Only for executables, scripts and installers. It fails closed to block when the containment component is not installed.
blockBlocked. The default.

A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

Type: string; matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-7[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$.

Whether a decision produces a local event.

Mode

How a policy's decisions take effect (#36).

The variants are declared from weakest to strongest, so the derived ordering ranks them. The "strictest" merge in #36 treats learning and audit as equally strong; that rule belongs to the merge code, not to this ordering.

ValueMeaning
disabledThe engine is not consulted. The device is reported as unprotected.
monitorEvaluate fully, allow everything, and report would-block decisions.
auditLike monitor, with a full event for every decision.
learningAudit, and report every would-block object as a learning candidate.
enforceDecisions take effect: blocked means blocked.

The class of object being evaluated. Scripts are script.<kind>.

What happens to processes a scheduled allow let run, when its schedule closes. The engine sends a directive; the agent and the tray act on it (#4, #11).

ValueMeaning
noneNothing: they keep running. The default.
warnWarn the user.
warn_then_terminateWarn the user, then terminate them after the grace period.

Operator

How a criterion compares the fact with its values (#32). Positive operators match if any value matches; negative operators (not_*) match if no value does, and never match a fact that is unknown.

ValueMeaning
equalsEqual to any value.
not_equalsEqual to none of the values.
starts_withStarts with any value. On paths, the value must end at a component boundary: C:\Tools does not match C:\ToolsX.
ends_withEnds with any value.
containsContains any value.
not_containsContains none of the values.
wildcardMatches any wildcard pattern.
not_wildcardMatches none of the wildcard patterns.
regexMatches any regular expression. Anchored at both ends, and run by a linear-time engine without look-around or backreferences.
not_regexMatches none of the regular expressions.
version_eqVersion equal to any value.
version_gtVersion greater than the value.
version_geVersion greater than or equal to the value.
version_ltVersion less than the value.
version_leVersion less than or equal to the value.
version_betweenVersion within [min, max], both inclusive. Takes exactly two values, the minimum first.
member_ofThe set holds any of the values (#33).
not_member_ofThe set holds none of the values (#33).
is_trueThe fact is true. Takes no values (#33).
is_falseThe fact is false. Takes no values (#33). On an unknown fact it is unknown, like every other test.
eqNumber, level or date equal to any value (#32).
neNumber, level or date equal to none of the values (#32).
gtGreater than the value (#32).
geGreater than or equal to the value (#32).
ltLess than the value (#32).
leLess than or equal to the value (#32).
betweenWithin [min, max], both inclusive. Takes exactly two values, the minimum first (#32).
ip_in_cidrThe address is in any of the CIDR blocks, such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 2001:db8::/32 (#32). On a set of addresses, any address may be.
ip_betweenThe address is in any of the ranges, written first-last or, for IPv4, a.b.c.first-last (#32).
ip_wildcardThe IPv4 address matches any whole-octet pattern, such as 10.*.*.* (#32).
any_ofThe set holds at least one of the values (#32). The same test as member_of.
all_ofThe set holds every one of the values (#32).
weekday_inThe day of the week is any of the values, mon to sun (#32).
time_betweenThe time of day is within [start, end), both HH:MM. A window whose end is before its start wraps midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 (#32).
date_betweenThe date is within [from, to], both YYYY-MM-DD and inclusive (#32).

How the matching rules of the ordinary rule sets are combined (#35).

The mandatory-deny tier and the implicit deny for unmatched files apply under every model (ADR 0004). The semantics of each model are in crate::precedence.

ValueMeaning

The settings apply to a subject when any entry holds; empty, the default, means no further limit. An effective policy has no policy.scope, so the hierarchy moves each contributing policy's scope and scopes here unexpanded (UnknownPolicy::scope_limit_of). The size is therefore linear in contributing policies, at most MAX_CONTRIBUTING_POLICIES (in hierarchy::limits) entries, and building an effective policy from valid policies never fails on it. Validation rejects it in a document it validates as authored, which writes policy.scope and unknown.scopes instead.

Palisade canonical event

One canonical event.

Field order here is the serialisation order, so Event::to_canonical_json is deterministic.

Schema: schemas/events/v1.json ($id https://github.com/jusso-dev/palisade/schemas/events/v1.json), version 1.2.0. Regenerate the schema with PALISADE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p palisade-proto --test events_schema, then these pages with cargo xtask docs generate.

modeEventModeno1.0.0The enforcement mode, where one applies.
nativeNativeno1.0.0OS-native enforcement details.
networkNetworkno1.1.0The network connection or request. Since 1.1.
outcomeOutcomeyes1.0.0What happened.
policyPolicyRefno1.0.0The Palisade policy and rule that decided, if known.

registryRegistryno1.1.0The registry key or value. Since 1.1.
